# `⊤` — Encode

`⊤Y` encodes nonnegative integers in binary, choosing enough digits for the largest value. The digits form a new last axis, so each number's digits are one row. Zero needs zero digits.

```apl
⊤5                ⍝ 1 0 1
⊤[2 5]ₓ           ⍝ [0 1 0 ⋄ 1 0 1]ₓ
```

`B⊤Y` represents numbers in bases `B`. A zero base retains the remaining quotient.

```apl
2 2 2 2⊤10         ⍝ 1 0 1 0
[0 60 60]ₓ⊤3661x   ⍝ [1 1 1]ₓ
```

A unit `B` gives residues. A vector `B` adds its digits as a new last axis, so the result's shape is `(⍴Y),⍴B`. Exact operands retain exact arithmetic.

```apl
9⊤15               ⍝ 6
9⊤⊂15              ⍝ ⊂6
10⊤12 34           ⍝ 2 4
2 2 2⊤3 5          ⍝ [0 1 1 ⋄ 1 0 1]
```

See [Decode](decode.qmd).
